questions.q: What is a Lightning Web Component built on, per this lesson, as distinct from the older Aura framework?
options: A Salesforce-proprietary scripting language unrelated to JavaScript
Modern web standards -- plain HTML, JavaScript, and the browser's native Custom Elements and Shadow DOM APIs
Java running on the Salesforce application server
A Flow-only declarative scripting layer
questions.explain: LWC is built on native web standards rather than a Salesforce-proprietary framework, and is now Salesforce's current recommended component model over the older Aura framework.

questions.q: What does the `.js-meta.xml` file control for `technicianJobBoard`?
options: The component's CSS styling
The Apex controller's governor limits
The component's test coverage percentage
The component's API version and where it is allowed to be used (e.g. record pages, app pages, tabs)
questions.explain: The .js-meta.xml metadata file declares the API version and the targets (record page, app page, tab, etc.) where the component can be placed -- without it, Setup won't offer the component as placeable.

options: Because all properties in LWC must be @api
Because @api makes a property load faster
Because the platform itself sets it automatically when the component is placed on a record page, requiring it to be public
Because recordId is a reserved keyword that requires @api
questions.explain: @api marks a property as public/settable from outside the component -- exactly what's needed since Lightning App Builder/the platform sets recordId automatically on a record page.

questions.q: Per this lesson, when is `@track` actually needed in modern LWC?
options: Only for mutating a property's contents in place inside an object or array, since simple field reassignment is already tracked automatically
On every property in every component, with no exceptions
Only on properties decorated with @api
Never -- @track has been completely removed from LWC
questions.explain: Modern LWC reactivity tracks simple field reassignment automatically; @track is mostly needed only for in-place mutation of an object or array's internal state, which technicianJobBoard doesn't do.

questions.q: Why doesn't `technicianJobBoard` use `connectedCallback()` to load its job data?
options: connectedCallback() cannot call Apex methods
LWC components are not allowed to have lifecycle hooks
connectedCallback() only runs once per org, not once per component instance
@wire already handles data loading declaratively and reactively, so an imperative call in a lifecycle hook isn't needed here
questions.explain: The component uses @wire(getMyJobs) for declarative, reactive data loading, which is the right fit here -- connectedCallback with an imperative call is reserved for cases where @wire's behavior doesn't fit, covered in Lesson 13.
